additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
examples: Eating only when alone because of fear that others will think strangely of the amount eaten.
Eating secretly after family members have gone to sleep.
Pretending to eat little in front of people, then binging when alone.
Locking the door or eating in a secret place like a car to avoid being seen eating.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

patient_info.stressor: Dennis moved from his family home in Latrobe into a shared off-campus apartment near school, excited about independence but thrown off by late study sessions, gaming nights, and the constant availability of pizza, snacks, and convenience food. Across 5 months, occasional overeating after basketball games or project deadlines shifted into episodes where he ate much more than he intended, quickly and alone in his room, then felt uncomfortably full and embarrassed afterward. The pattern had not yet derailed his classes or robotics commitments, but it bothered him because it clashed with his organized, performance-driven identity. He booked an appointment through campus counseling after completing an anonymous online screening that suggested his eating episodes warranted a psychiatric evaluation.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: On nights after a project deadline or when the apartment has leftover pizza around, I can end up eating a whole small pizza plus chips and cereal in my room, way more than I planned or than my roommates would eat for a normal dinner.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: What really made me come in is that once I start eating like that, it feels like I hit some switch and I keep going even while part of me is thinking, Dennis, just stop already.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
S051.manifestation: During those times I eat fast, like standing at my desk between homework and a game, barely tasting it and realizing afterward that the food is gone in just a few minutes.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
S052.manifestation: I usually stop only when my stomach feels tight and heavy, like I need to lie down for a while and I’m uncomfortable sitting at my desk.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
S054.manifestation: I’ll eat a normal-ish amount if my roommates are in the kitchen, then take extra stuff back to my room later because I don’t want them seeing how much I’m actually eating.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
S055.manifestation: Afterward I feel embarrassed and kind of grossed out with myself, especially because I’m usually pretty disciplined with school and robotics and it makes me feel like I’m not in control.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: Since early in the semester, it’s been happening most weeks, usually one night and sometimes two when deadlines or apartment food pile up. I’d say that pattern has been steady for at least the last three or four months.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’m still making it to class and robotics, but I sometimes feel distracted or sluggish the next morning and spend extra time worrying about whether my roommates noticed. It bothers me more than it has actually knocked me off track.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about five months, since I moved into the off-campus apartment.
